title: Solar Generator With Panels Included (2026): How to Compare 1 kWh Kits
short_title: The solar panel number every kit box leaves out
summary: A solar generator with panels included is a portable power station and a folding solar panel sold in one box. This video compares the 1 kWh-class kits on the makers' own US stores (ALLPOWERS, BLUETTI, Jackery, EcoFlow, Anker) on the four numbers that decide them: battery, inverter, panel watts in the box, and the station's maximum solar input.
short_summary: A folding solar panel delivers about 60-75% of its rating in good sun, so check two numbers on any solar generator kit: the panel watts in the box and the station's maximum solar input.

long.say: A solar generator with panels included is a portable power station sold in one box with a folding solar panel. In this video: how to compare the one-kilowatt-hour kits, using the numbers on each maker's own US store. long.say: Judge any kit on four numbers. First, the battery, in watt-hours, and whether its cells are LiFePO4, which last thousands of cycles. Second, the inverter watts, which decide what you can run at once. Third, the panel watts in the box. And fourth, the one most people miss: the station's maximum solar input. That is the ceiling on how much panel you can ever add.

long.say: Here's what the box won't tell you. A folding panel delivers roughly sixty to seventy-five percent of its rating in good sun. So a two-hundred-watt panel puts back about six hundred to seven hundred fifty watt-hours on a clear day with five peak-sun hours. That's most of a one-kilowatt-hour battery, but not all of it.

slide.note: 200 W panel × 5 peak-sun hours ≈ 600–750 Wh on a clear day

long.say: Here are the one-kilowatt-hour kits on the makers' own stores. They all land between about one thousand and eleven hundred fifty watt-hours, and most ship a two-hundred-watt panel. Two stand out. ALLPOWERS' P1800 kit ships a four-hundred-watt panel, twice what the others include. And BLUETTI's AC180 kit has the most battery, at eleven hundred fifty-two watt-hours. Anker's C1000 Gen 2 has the strongest inverter, at two thousand watts.

slide.foot: Specs from each maker's US page, read 2026-10-24 to 2026-11-05

long.say: So which one? If you want the kit that refills itself fastest out of the box, the ALLPOWERS P1800 with its four-hundred-watt SP037 panel. Just know that panel weighs about eighteen and a half kilograms, so it's a two-hand carry. If you want the most battery and a lighter panel, the BLUETTI AC180 two-hundred-watt kit. Stock and pre-order dates change, so check the description for where each one stands today.

items: Most panel in the box: ALLPOWERS P1800 + SP037
400 W panel (18.5 kg); the station takes up to 650 W
Most battery: BLUETTI AC180 + 200 W
1,152 Wh LiFePO4; takes up to 500 W of panel

long.say: Need more? For two kilowatt-hours of home backup, BLUETTI's Elite 200 V2 with a two-hundred-watt panel, which can take up to a thousand watts of panel later. The ALLPOWERS S2000 Pro kit gives you a twenty-four-hundred-watt inverter, but on N-M-C cells, which wear out sooner than LiFePO4. And for phones, lights and a fan over a weekend, a small kit of two hundred fifty to three hundred watt-hours is enough.

long.say: Two checks before you buy. Price the station and the panel separately: some kits cost exactly the same as the two parts, and at least one costs hundreds more. And if you add panels later, match their voltage to the station's solar input range, or the station won't charge from them.
